author: agent:claude-code
message: Restructure the accidental first draft into the repo's real layout (DESIGN.md: platforms, per-host overrides, home-manager layer with feature modules, dev-utils), keeping the drafted nodes by renaming/moving/merging so their history carries over.; Adopt the layering the code already keeps, and record the decisions made while building Hyprland, the vgsquid servers and the AMD setup, so they're flagged if what they rest on changes. (proposal 01a122bb-24bf-7339-812e-77eda7c86b67, proposed by agent:claude-code, accepted by user)

name: Composition
intent: The master flake: the table of every machine (hostname, system, nixType, user, state version) and the entry points that turn it into nixosConfigurations, darwinConfigurations and homeConfigurations through each platform's sub-flake, plus the justfiles and scripts that build, switch and inspect them.

text: What every platform's system config shares: usrlib (the mk*Option helpers every module declares its options with), the nix settings (flakes, caches, weekly gc) and home-manager wired in as a system module.

reason: home/ and home/modules/ are one layer: the home-manager entry point and the platform-agnostic core it imports

text: The home-manager layer every machine shares: the user's shell, terminal, editors, git, languages and CLI tools, each a feature module with options a platform or host can override, and the per-platform home trees it pulls in by nixType and hostname.
The bun JavaScript runtime and package manager, with its bunfig settings.

name: claude-code
intent: Claude Code from claude-code-nix, with isolated account profiles: a claude-<name> command per profile, one bound to bare claude, and a shared CLAUDE.md.

name: editor
intent: The editors: vim, neovim (the default $EDITOR, with its live-edited lua config), Zed in vim mode, and the vimrc VS Code's vim extension reads.

name: freerdp
intent: The FreeRDP client with saved hosts, each an rdp-<name> command (and on macOS a dockable app reading its password from the Keychain).

name: git
intent: git with the user's identity and delta as its pager, and the GitHub CLI.

name: java
intent: A JDK (Temurin) for Java work.

name: rustup
intent: rustup as the Rust toolchain manager, with CARGO_HOME and RUSTUP_HOME in the home directory.

name: shell
intent: zsh and bash with completion, autosuggestions and syntax highlighting, the shell hotkeys, direnv with nix-direnv, and the fragments other modules add to the rc files.

name: ssh
intent: The ssh client config, with keep-alives.

name: term
intent: The terminal: kitty (with its own colour scheme), zellij as the multiplexer that starts with every shell, yazi as the file manager, starship as the prompt, each with its live-edited config.

name: NixOS
intent: Bare-metal NixOS machines: the sub-flake that builds them, the system modules they choose from, the NixOS-only home modules, and one node per host.

text: What every NixOS machine is built from, each piece a switch a host can flip: boot, audio, connectivity, login and desktop sessions (Plasma, Hyprland), graphics (AMD and NVIDIA), input devices, the base environment, and the headless server profile.

name: Hyprland
intent: A Hyprland desktop assembled piece by piece (no desktop environment): waybar, fuzzel, mako, hyprlock, hypridle, hyprpaper, the keyring, Thunar, udiskie, and Kanagawa Dragon theming for Qt and GTK, all live-edited. Built and validated, not yet run on hardware.

name: Headless
intent: The home side of a headless server: no GUI apps. Pairs with core.headless on the system side.

name: Tailscale
intent: tailscaled on a NixOS host: its own tailnet node, Tailscale SSH advertised, tailscale0 trusted.

name: Apps
intent: The desktop apps NixOS machines install by default (a headless host turns them off): Steam, Vivaldi, VS Code, Discord, Spotify, Prism Launcher and Proton Pass.

text: The main desktop: Radeon RX 7800 XT with LACT and ROCm, Hyprland as the daily session with Plasma kept as a fallback, and the keyring forced for Chromium-based apps.

name: vgnixmini
intent: A Plasma desktop on the defaults. Waits on its hardware-configuration.nix, which is generated on the machine.

name: vgsquid-azul
intent: A headless server with a Radeon RX 7800 XT for GPU compute (ROCm, LACT), reached over Tailscale and OpenSSH. Waits on its hardware-configuration.nix.

name: vgsquid-onyx
intent: vgsquid-azul's twin: a headless server with a Radeon RX 7800 XT for GPU compute, reached over Tailscale and OpenSSH. Waits on its hardware-configuration.nix.

name: NixOS-WSL
intent: NixOS running under WSL2 on the Windows host: its sub-flake, its modules (base environment, tailscale) and its host.

text: The WSL base: the distro's user and hostname, zsh, nix-ld for the VS Code server, and fonts for WSLg apps.

name: vgwsl2
intent: The WSL distro on vghydra: its own tailnet node, and the same Claude Code profiles as vgmacbook.

name: nix-darwin
intent: macOS through nix-darwin: its sub-flake, its system modules (Homebrew as the source of GUI and App Store apps, hotkeys, an optional window manager and status bar) and macOS-only home modules (keyboard layout, Homebrew aliases, the Tailscale CLI), and its host.

text: The macOS base: the primary user, Touch ID for sudo, Dock, Finder, trackpad and keyboard defaults, fonts, and the hidutil key remap that is re-applied at every login.

name: Apps
intent: Dockable .app bundles built from shell commands, among them an RDP <host>.app for each FreeRDP host that asks for one.

name: vgmacbook
intent: The MacBook: its Homebrew casks and Mac App Store apps, FreeRDP to vghydra, Tailscale, and the personal and work Claude Code profiles.

name: Dev utils
intent: Nix examples to learn from and flake templates to start new projects with; not part of any machine.

text: The smallest dev-shell flake, loaded by direnv.
A flake with an FHS environment, for software that expects a conventional Linux filesystem layout.
An example of building with stdenv, kept as a reference and deliberately not built (flake.nobuild.nix).
The template a new Python project starts from: a flake with a Python dev shell.

Every module declares its options with usrlib's mk*Option helpers and does nothing unless enabled; a host's own folder (nix/<platform>/<host> for the system, home/<platform>/<host> for home) only flips and overrides them.

Application config files live as raw files in a module's *.d folder, linked into place with mkOutOfStoreSymlink so an edit applies without a rebuild; nix generates a config file only when it must interpolate store paths.
Keyboard layers (DESIGN.md): the compositor and system own meta/SUPER+*; apps, terminals and multiplexers keep ctrl, alt and the F-keys.
A home module under home/modules works on every platform; anything platform-only lives in home/<platform>/modules.
Shared doesn't use Composition: Composition builds on it
Home doesn't use Shared or Composition: they build on it

title: Hyprland config is raw live-edited files, not home-manager's hyprland module
body: home-manager's wayland.windowManager.hyprland generates ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf, which would collide with hypr.d linked out of store. The compositor comes from the NixOS module (programs.hyprland, withUWSM); everything else is raw config in hypr.d, waybar.d, fuzzel.d, mako.d, qt6ct.d and uwsm.d, started from autostart.conf rather than systemd user units so none of it leaks into the Plasma session. Validated with Hyprland 0.52.2 --verify-config and fuzzel --check-config; not yet run on hardware.

title: Plasma stays as a fallback session beside Hyprland until Hyprland has run on the 7800 XT
body: core.desktop.sessions became a list so SDDM offers both. A broken Hyprland config or session environment then never locks the user out. Plasma adds 59 KDE packages (visible in fuzzel) but none of its theming, wallet or portals reach the Hyprland session. Drop it with core.desktop.sessions = [ "hyprland" ] once Hyprland is proven on the machine.

title: gnome-keyring as the Secret Service, Chromium apps forced onto it
body: Proton Pass is the password manager, but Electron and Chromium apps (Proton Pass itself, VS Code, Vivaldi) keep their own tokens in the system keyring, and they don't recognise Hyprland as a desktop, so they fall back to obfuscated plaintext. gnome-keyring runs standalone (unlocked by SDDM's PAM) and the three apps get --password-store=gnome-libsecret on vgkraken (verified in the built wrappers). Its gcr-ssh-agent is turned off: gpg-agent is already the SSH agent (core/env.nix), and two agents would race for SSH_AUTH_SOCK.

title: Headless is two switches, core.headless (system) and nixtype.headless (home)
body: The repo also builds standalone homeConfigurations for option inspection, and those load only home/. Setting home options from the NixOS module (home-manager.users.<user>) would make that inspection show GUI apps that aren't installed. Same split as vgmacbook's tailscale (cask in nix/, alias in home/). Open alternative: a `headless` fact in the flake's configurations table passed through specialArgs, so both trees default from one value.

title: AMD GPUs get LACT with overdrive and ROCm OpenCL as opt-in switches
body: core.graphics.amd: early KMS and 32-bit graphics always; lact.enable adds lactd plus hardware.amdgpu.overdrive (RDNA3 fan control needs the ppfeaturemask), opencl.enable adds ROCm, clinfo and the render/video groups. All three 7800 XT hosts turn both on. ROCm, the kernel and LACT come from the binary cache (dry-run build), so nothing large compiles. NVIDIA options stay, now off by default.

title: NVIDIA session variables were written for a GPU vgkraken no longer has
body: env-hyprland first exported LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia and __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia for the old PRIME setup; on the 7800 XT they would break VA-API and GLX. Removed when the hardware was confirmed. Lesson: confirm a host's target hardware before writing GPU-specific session environment.
